comparator.name: Dentistry (Tandheelkunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations set out a Dutch-taught, three-year curriculum of 60 EC per year, with no tracks, minor or elective space. The assessment plan details the supervised bachelor thesis and patient care in the Bachelor Clinic.
components: Variaties in groei, gedrag en ontwikkeling

core: Human anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, cell biology, immunity, pharmacology and disease mechanisms
Epidemiology, public health, health behaviour and prevention
Lifespan development, patient behaviour, psychological assessment and health communication
Experimental methods, statistics, evidence synthesis and evidence-based health research

trace: introduces research design, measurement, sampling, experiments, surveys and inferential statistics for empirical health questions
studies disease distribution, determinants, evidence appraisal and population-health decisions relevant to prevention, while not teaching oral epidemiology
Uses medical images, anatomical drawing and specimen-based observation to relate structure to function in human body systems.
examines drug targets, physiological effects, therapeutic use and toxicity as a general treatment-science foundation rather than dental pharmacology
studies innate and adaptive immunity, host-pathogen interactions and tissue damage relevant to infectious disease generally, without an oral focus
analyses cellular and physiological disease mechanisms through clinical cases, providing general pathophysiology rather than dental diagnosis
Connects brain anatomy, comparative neurobiology and the regulation of behaviour, including sleep and mood.
Studies how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal-directed behaviour using cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
examines memory, attention, executive functions and cognitive control relevant to patient understanding and decision-making
Introduces cells, macromolecules, metabolism, heredity and gene expression through the analysis of scientific experiments and literature.
introduces psychology, brain systems and behaviour and is the formal foundation for later cognition and health-psychology courses
Studies primarily eukaryotic cell structure, regulation and signalling, including gene expression, cell division and disease processes.
studies normal human physiological systems and structure-function relations as a healthy-body foundation
Links biomolecules, enzyme kinetics and metabolic pathways to the analysis of biochemical disease mechanisms.
provides laboratory work with blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics; it is not a preclinical dental-skills laboratory
studies molecular pathology, human genetics, inflammation, tissue injury and repair as mechanisms of disease without dental pathology
examines social cognition, attitudes, interpersonal behaviour and social influence relevant to patient interaction
develops experimental design and multivariate statistics for behavioural and health research
studies health behaviour, sociocultural influences, psychological intervention and communication in medical settings
teaches psychological assessment and psychotherapeutic approaches relevant to understanding patient needs, not clinical dental assessment
develops systematic review, meta-analysis, effect-size calculation and evidence synthesis for evidence-based health decisions
studies cognitive and social development across the lifespan, providing context for age-sensitive health behaviour and communication
Studies framing, argumentation and persuasion ethics through public communication projects on sustainable behaviour. These methods can inform prevention messaging.

alternatives.label: Biomedical foundations, public health & health behaviour
alternatives.concept: Study how the human body works, how disease develops and how behaviour and social conditions affect health. Combine laboratory science with epidemiology, health psychology and methods for evaluating research.
alternatives.labelReason: Human biology and disease mechanisms form the science sequence. Epidemiology, health psychology and evidence synthesis connect it to prevention and patient behaviour.
progression: The life-science gateway precedes anatomy, cell biology, physiology, laboratory work and advanced biomedical courses. The brain and behaviour gateway precedes advanced cognition and psychology. Introductory research design and statistics lead into experimental methods and evidence synthesis.

candidates.label: Oral science, dental diagnosis, restorative treatment and clinical practice

selection.assessment: One related programme combines biomedical science, prevention, health behaviour and evidence appraisal. An oral-science or clinical dentistry option would require a sustained sequence in oral anatomy, dental disease, preclinical techniques, treatment planning and supervised patient care.

blocks: Both introduce cellular and molecular foundations of human health. Groningen develops these foundations within dental training.
Both develop knowledge of normal bodily function. UCR focuses on adult organ systems and homeostasis.
Both draw on mechanisms of infection and immunity to explain compromised health. Groningen applies these concepts in oral healthcare.
Both consider how disease mechanisms affect health. The UCR cases concern systemic disease and clinical reasoning across organ systems.
Public health, prevention and health behaviour
Both address prevention. UCR studies disease patterns, risk and interventions at population level. Groningen applies prevention to oral health.
Both examine how behaviour and social context shape health and care. UCR includes interviews and general medical settings. Groningen uses oral-health cases.
Both consider how development and behaviour change across life stages. Groningen applies this to dental growth and care.
Both introduce scientific inquiry. UCR adds a team project that collects and analyses data.
Both develop empirical research skills. UCR focuses on experimental design and multivariable analysis.
Both evaluate and synthesise research. UCR teaches systematic review and meta-analysis. Groningen requires an individual supervised bachelor thesis in dentistry.
Both include reflection on professional development. UCR develops academic writing, self-management and civic engagement.
Oral science, dental technique and clinical-care gaps
Groningen students assess and treat patients under supervision in the Bachelor Clinic.

notes.text: The UCR option shares foundations in human biology, prevention, health behaviour and research. Groningen also requires oral anatomy and disease science, dental materials and radiography, preclinical skills, treatment planning and supervised patient care. The UCR option does not lead to qualification as a dentist.

audience.programmeDescription: Dentistry at the University of Groningen combines human and oral science with technical skills and patient care. Students practise on artificial jaws and teeth, progress to supervised care and complete a bachelor thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in human biology, disease, prevention and health behaviour. Groningen builds on these foundations with dental diagnosis, restorative techniques and supervised treatment.
